question.text: The financial markets enable efficient transfer and allocation of resources. Who acts as INTERMEDIARY between providers of surplus funds and users of funds per Ch 1.1.1?

answer.text: Only the Ministry of Finance directly disburses surplus funds
Banks, financial institutions, mutual funds and insurance companies channelize surplus funds from lenders to users
Only RBI and SEBI — the regulators themselves

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.1.1, intermediaries such as banks, financial institutions, mutual funds and insurance companies channelize surplus funds from providers (households, businesses, governments with surplus) to users (governments, businesses, households needing funds). The Trap: Option A confuses policy with intermediation. Option C narrows to P2P. Option D conflates regulation with intermediation. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to XII (Securities Markets Foundation). Understanding the intermediary layer helps SIAs trace funds flow when an SE is funded through an intermediated channel (e.g., a mutual fund for SSE or an AIF). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Map the donor-to-beneficiary funds-flow diagram at engagement start: Donor → Intermediary (MF-for-SSE/AIF/Bank) → SE → Project → Beneficiary. Each arrow is a documentation point for SAS-1100 assurance.
